result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give pasteable CSS, stay within the licence limits and pick one option with reasons. B fits the zero-budget, small-page brief more closely: it downloads no font files at all, states what it assumed (Latin script, screens only), and admits rendering will differ by device, so the team should test on a real cheap Android phone. A is strong too, with a solid Inter subsetting and self-hosting setup and a good warning about the Google Fonts CDN, but it states which system fonts each device gets with less hedging, and its Arial-based fallback font won't work on Android, which usually doesn't ship Arial. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A sticks closely to the zero-budget, small-page-weight brief. It uses only system fonts, adds a zero-byte serif display stack for marketing, and is frank that rendering will differ by device. B offers a more distinctive marketing option with explicit licence status (Inter is under the SIL OFL), subsetting commands, preloading and a metric-matched fallback. However, it states device font availability with less hedging and runs longer, so the two answers' strengths roughly balance out.
